title: Checkout failures during flash-sale traffic spike — db.pool.exhausted
symptoms: checkout-api alerts fired for elevated 5xx during a flash-sale traffic spike. checkout-handler logs showed repeated `db.pool.exhausted in_use=10 size=10` immediately followed by `checkout.payment_failed order_id=... err=ConnectionPoolExhausted`. Customers reported checkout failures and spinning carts. On-call initially suspected the database itself was undersized for peak load.
root_cause: Not fully identified at the time. On-call verified actual connection counts on the database side were well below its real ceiling, ruling out true DB capacity limits, but could not determine why the application-side pool still drained completely under load. Closed as mitigated via pool size increase and load shedding; true root cause was left as 'connection pool sizing marginal for peak traffic' with a follow-up investigation ticket that was never completed.

resolution_steps.action: Confirmed the alert signal via checkout-handler logs
resolution_steps.outcome: Verified repeated db.pool.exhausted in_use=10 size=10 during the traffic spike window

resolution_steps.action: Checked database-side connection metrics to rule out real DB capacity limits
resolution_steps.outcome: DB connection count was far below its actual ceiling — database itself was not the bottleneck

resolution_steps.action: Increased the application connection pool size as a stopgap
resolution_steps.outcome: Reduced frequency of db.pool.exhausted during the remainder of the spike, but did not eliminate it under sustained peak load

resolution_steps.action: Enabled request-level load shedding at checkout-api during peak windows
resolution_steps.outcome: Reduced customer-visible failure rate by rejecting excess requests early instead of failing deep in checkout-handler

resolution_steps.action: Filed a follow-up ticket to investigate why pool exhaustion still occurs at the new, larger pool size under peak load
resolution_steps.outcome: Incident closed as mitigated; follow-up investigation was never completed and the underlying cause remains undetermined

title: Customers report slow checkout — latency dashboards green, no alert fired
symptoms: Support tickets and Slack reports described checkout 'taking forever' or the spinner hanging, but the checkout latency dashboard (`metrics.latency name=checkout.duration agg=avg`) stayed within normal bounds the entire time and no alert fired. On-call was paged by a manager escalation rather than an alert, checked `api.request` / `api.error` logs and saw no elevated error rate, and confirmed `CheckoutAPI.get_health` returned healthy throughout.
root_cause: Unable to reproduce or correlate against any internal signal — every monitored aggregate looked nominal for the entire reported window. Closed as 'could not reproduce — dashboards nominal', with a note for next time to collect specific order_ids from affected customers so individual checkout.start/checkout.success timestamps could be traced directly.

resolution_steps.action: Reviewed the checkout latency dashboard for the reported time window
resolution_steps.outcome: Average latency (metrics.latency name=checkout.duration agg=avg) was within normal range — no anomaly visible

resolution_steps.action: Spot-checked api.request and api.error logs for the affected time range
resolution_steps.outcome: No elevated error rate or unusual err= values found

resolution_steps.action: Checked CheckoutAPI.get_health status over the window
resolution_steps.outcome: Health checks passed continuously; no service-level degradation indicated

resolution_steps.action: Requested specific order_ids or timestamps from support to trace individual checkout.start/checkout.success pairs
resolution_steps.outcome: No usable order_ids were provided before the reporting customers churned off the topic

resolution_steps.action: Closed the incident as could not reproduce
resolution_steps.outcome: No fix applied; recommendation left to capture order_ids on any future recurrence of this complaint

title: payment.retry storm during payment-gateway provider outage
symptoms: PagerDuty fired on an elevated `checkout.payment_failed` rate. Logs showed repeated `payment.retry order_id=... attempt=n/8 backoff=...s` climbing through all 8 attempts, followed by `payment.exhausted order_id=... attempts=8` and `checkout.payment_failed order_id=... err=GatewayTimeout`. Customers saw checkout errors and support was flooded with tickets.
root_cause: The upstream payment-gateway provider suffered a partial outage, causing `PaymentClient._call_gateway` to exceed `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` on a large fraction of calls. `PaymentClient.charge` exhausted all `PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES` (8) attempts with exponential backoff before giving up, producing the payment.exhausted signal for affected orders.

resolution_steps.action: Confirmed provider-side outage via the gateway status page and correlated GatewayTimeout errors in PaymentClient._call_gateway
resolution_steps.outcome: Root cause identified as an upstream provider issue, not an application bug

resolution_steps.action: Communicated the outage status to support so agents could set customer expectations
resolution_steps.outcome: Reduced duplicate ticket volume during the outage

resolution_steps.action: Monitored payment.retry and payment.exhausted rates until the provider recovered
resolution_steps.outcome: payment.retry volume dropped back to baseline once the provider status page confirmed resolution

resolution_steps.action: Added a dashboard alert on sustained payment.exhausted rate to page on-call faster during future provider-side degradations
resolution_steps.outcome: Future gateway outages of this scale will be detected within minutes instead of via customer tickets

title: fulfillment.queue.full — orders backing up during promo traffic
symptoms: Logs showed `fulfillment.enqueued order_id=... depth=...` climbing steadily throughout a promo push, then `fulfillment.queue.full depth=5000 max=5000` followed by a batch of `checkout.enqueue_failed order_id=... err=QueueFull`. Checkout itself succeeded (payment charged) for these orders but fulfillment enqueue failed.
root_cause: fulfillment-worker, the downstream queue consumer, was under-scaled for the promo traffic volume. Its consumption rate fell behind FulfillmentQueue.enqueue's arrival rate, filling the queue to QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH (5000).

resolution_steps.action: Checked FulfillmentQueue.depth() trend leading up to the incident
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed a steady climb to max over ~40 minutes, not a sudden spike — consistent with a capacity mismatch rather than a burst

resolution_steps.action: Scaled up the fulfillment-worker deployment
resolution_steps.outcome: Consumption rate exceeded arrival rate; queue depth began draining

resolution_steps.action: Temporarily raised QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH to give fulfillment-worker headroom to catch up
resolution_steps.outcome: No further checkout.enqueue_failed errors for the remainder of the promo window

resolution_steps.action: Reverted QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH to 5000 after the promo window closed and added a pre-promo fulfillment-worker scaling step to the promo runbook
resolution_steps.outcome: Queue depth returned to normal baseline; future promos scale fulfillment-worker proactively

title: Checkout failures spike after deploy — PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES misconfigured to 1
symptoms: checkout.payment_failed rate jumped immediately after a routine deploy. Logs showed `payment.exhausted order_id=... attempts=1` right after the corresponding `payment.call` line, with no `payment.retry` entries in between. The `config.loaded` log line on the new pods read `payment_max_retries=1` instead of the expected 8.
root_cause: The deploy shipped a config.py change that accidentally set PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES=1 during an unrelated config refactor, so transient gateway blips that would normally succeed on retry now failed checkout immediately.

resolution_steps.action: Diffed the new config.loaded log output against the previous deploy's baseline
resolution_steps.outcome: Found payment_max_retries=1 instead of the expected 8

resolution_steps.action: Reverted the offending deploy
resolution_steps.command: git revert <deploy-commit> && kubectl rollout restart deployment checkout-handler
resolution_steps.outcome: PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES restored to 8; checkout.payment_failed rate returned to baseline within minutes

resolution_steps.action: Added a config validation check to the deploy pipeline asserting PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES stays within an expected 5-10 range
resolution_steps.outcome: Prevents future accidental low-retry deploys from reaching production

title: db.pool.exhausted immediately after deploy — DB_POOL_SIZE typo
symptoms: Within minutes of a config cleanup deploy, `db.pool.exhausted in_use=3 size=3` appeared under completely normal, non-peak traffic. checkout-handler began throwing ConnectionPoolExhausted almost immediately — unlike a load-driven exhaustion, this happened at ordinary traffic levels.
root_cause: The deploy's config.py change set DB_POOL_SIZE=3 instead of the intended 10, a fat-fingered edit during an unrelated config cleanup. The undersized pool exhausted under normal load within minutes.

resolution_steps.action: Checked the config.loaded log line on freshly deployed pods
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed pool_size=3 instead of the expected 10

resolution_steps.action: Rolled back the deploy
resolution_steps.outcome: DB_POOL_SIZE restored to 10; db.pool.exhausted stopped immediately

resolution_steps.action: Added a CI smoke-test assertion on the config.loaded pool_size value before deploys are allowed to promote
resolution_steps.outcome: Catches config typos of this kind before they reach production

title: Checkout API returning TLS errors — ingress certificate expired
symptoms: `api.error path=/checkout order_id=... err=...` entries showed TLS handshake failures at the load balancer in front of checkout-api; many requests never reached CheckoutAPI.post_checkout at all. An alert fired on the checkout-api 5xx rate as clients failed to connect.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for the checkout-api ingress expired; the automated renewal job had failed silently roughly two weeks earlier without alerting anyone.

resolution_steps.action: Checked the certificate expiry against the checkout-api ingress endpoint
resolution_steps.command: openssl s_client -connect checkout-api.internal:443 -servername checkout-api.internal | openssl x509 -noout -dates
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed notAfter was in the past

resolution_steps.action: Manually issued and deployed a new certificate
resolution_steps.command: ccloud cert issue --service checkout-api && kubectl apply -f checkout-api-tls-secret.yaml
resolution_steps.outcome: TLS handshake errors stopped immediately after rollout

resolution_steps.action: Fixed the auto-renewal cronjob and added an alert 14 days before certificate expiry
resolution_steps.outcome: Prevents future silent renewal failures from reaching expiry

title: Elevated GatewayTimeout errors from payment-gateway — single-AZ network ACL regression
symptoms: A subset of PaymentClient._call_gateway calls began timing out with GatewayTimeout; payment.retry attempts appeared but usually succeeded within a few attempts rather than exhausting. checkout.payment_failed rate rose modestly and was concentrated in requests originating from one availability zone.
root_cause: A network team firewall/ACL change the previous day had blocked a subset of outbound traffic from one AZ to the payment-gateway provider's endpoint, causing connection timeouts that PaymentClient surfaced as GatewayTimeout.

resolution_steps.action: Correlated the geographic distribution of checkout.payment_failed against availability zone
resolution_steps.outcome: Found impact was isolated to a single AZ, not global — pointed away from a provider-wide outage

resolution_steps.action: Asked the network team to review recent firewall/ACL changes affecting that AZ
resolution_steps.outcome: Identified an ACL change from the previous day restricting egress to the payment-gateway provider

resolution_steps.action: Network team reverted the ACL change
resolution_steps.outcome: GatewayTimeout rate in the affected AZ returned to baseline within minutes

resolution_steps.action: Added a synthetic health check exercising payment-gateway connectivity from each AZ
resolution_steps.outcome: Catches future per-AZ connectivity regressions before they affect customer checkouts

title: checkout-handler pods evicted — disk full from leftover debug logging
symptoms: CheckoutAPI.get_health checks started failing intermittently as checkout-handler pods were evicted. `kubectl describe pod` showed DiskPressure evictions. There was no unusual application-level log signal — the issue was infrastructure-level disk exhaustion, not a code path problem.
root_cause: A debug-level logging flag enabled during a prior investigation was never reverted, filling local pod disk with verbose logs over several days until kubelet evicted pods under DiskPressure.

resolution_steps.action: Checked node conditions for evicted pods
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed DiskPressure-triggered eviction, not an application crash

resolution_steps.action: Reverted the logging level and cleared accumulated log files
resolution_steps.outcome: Disk usage dropped sharply; pods stopped being evicted

resolution_steps.action: Added a log-level revert reminder to the debugging runbook and a disk-usage alert at 80%
resolution_steps.outcome: Prevents future debug-logging leftovers from silently filling disk

title: checkout-handler CrashLoopBackOff after deploy — broken import
symptoms: Immediately after a deploy, all checkout-handler pods entered CrashLoopBackOff. checkout-api returned 503s for every request, and `api.error path=/checkout` showed connection-refused failures rather than application-level errors, indicating checkout-handler itself was never coming up.
root_cause: The deploy included a change to checkout.py with a broken import referencing a module path that didn't exist in the built container image, causing CheckoutHandler's process to fail at startup before it could serve any traffic.

resolution_steps.action: Checked crashed pod logs for the startup failure
resolution_steps.outcome: Found a Python ImportError in checkout.py at process startup

resolution_steps.action: Rolled back the deploy immediately
resolution_steps.outcome: Pods returned to Running; checkout-api 503s stopped within about 2 minutes

resolution_steps.action: Fixed the import in a follow-up PR and added a container smoke-test that imports all application modules during the build
resolution_steps.outcome: Prevents future broken-import deploys from reaching production

title: fulfillment.queue.full — fulfillment-worker deployment down, zero drain
symptoms: FulfillmentQueue.depth() climbed steadily with zero drain over roughly an hour, eventually hitting `fulfillment.queue.full depth=5000 max=5000` and triggering `checkout.enqueue_failed` errors. Unlike a normal traffic-driven fill, the enqueue rate itself was unremarkable — nothing was consuming from the queue at all.
root_cause: The fulfillment-worker deployment (the downstream queue consumer, external to checkout_service) had crashed and its pods failed to restart due to an unrelated infrastructure issue, so nothing was consuming from the queue while checkout continued enqueueing normally.

resolution_steps.action: Checked fulfillment-worker pod status
resolution_steps.outcome: Found 0/5 pods Ready

resolution_steps.action: Restarted the fulfillment-worker deployment
resolution_steps.outcome: Pods came back healthy; queue began draining immediately

resolution_steps.action: Monitored FulfillmentQueue.depth() until it returned to near-zero baseline
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed full recovery; queue held orders rather than dropping them, so no orders were lost

resolution_steps.action: Added a fulfillment-worker liveness alert independent of the queue-depth alert
resolution_steps.outcome: Catches future consumer outages before the queue has a chance to fill

title: Intermittent checkout-api 502s — readiness probe too aggressive
symptoms: A low-grade but persistent trickle of `api.error path=/checkout` entries with connection-reset style failures appeared over several days. CheckoutAPI.get_health passed on every manual check, yet Kubernetes kept cycling pods out of rotation.
root_cause: The readiness probe timeout was shorter than CheckoutHandler's occasional slow-path latency, so Kubernetes intermittently marked healthy pods NotReady and cycled them out of rotation mid-request during normal (non-incident-level) latency variance.

resolution_steps.action: Correlated 502 timestamps against pod readiness transition events
resolution_steps.outcome: Found readiness probe flapping coincided exactly with the 502 trickle, not application errors

resolution_steps.action: Increased the readiness probe timeout and failure threshold
resolution_steps.outcome: Readiness flapping stopped and the 502 trickle disappeared

resolution_steps.action: Documented the probe tuning rationale in the on-call runbook
resolution_steps.outcome: Prevents future over-aggressive probe settings from being reintroduced

title: payment.retry storm amplified by too-aggressive backoff configuration
symptoms: During a minor payment-gateway blip, `payment.retry` volume was far higher than the size of the blip should have caused — retries were hammering the gateway in rapid succession rather than backing off, and `payment.exhausted` counts climbed faster than expected for the underlying issue.
root_cause: A prior config change had set PAYMENT_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS too low (0.05s instead of the intended 0.5s), so PaymentClient.charge's exponential backoff barely delayed between attempts, amplifying load on an already-degraded gateway.

resolution_steps.action: Checked config.loaded log values against documented defaults
resolution_steps.outcome: Found PAYMENT_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS=0.05 instead of the intended 0.5

resolution_steps.action: Corrected the backoff base delay
resolution_steps.outcome: Restored proper exponential backoff spacing between retry attempts

resolution_steps.action: Redeployed checkout-handler with the corrected config
resolution_steps.outcome: Retry volume against the gateway dropped to levels appropriate for the blip's actual severity

title: Payment failure spike went unpaged — alert threshold set too high
symptoms: A moderate, sustained increase in `checkout.payment_failed` rate persisted for over an hour with no page. It was found only through a manual dashboard review; the configured alert threshold for that metric had been set for a much larger-scale incident and never revisited.
root_cause: The alert threshold for checkout.payment_failed rate was originally configured for a much larger incident scale and never revisited as normal traffic grew; a real, moderate-severity payment issue stayed under threshold for its entire duration.

resolution_steps.action: Reviewed historical checkout.payment_failed rate distribution to pick a realistic alert threshold
resolution_steps.outcome: Determined the existing threshold was roughly 10x higher than any real moderate incident would reach

resolution_steps.action: Lowered the alert threshold and added an intermediate warning-level tier
resolution_steps.outcome: Future incidents of this scale will page on-call instead of requiring manual dashboard discovery

resolution_steps.action: Backfilled a retroactive review of the missed window
resolution_steps.outcome: Confirmed the underlying payment issue had self-resolved and no further remediation was needed for that specific occurrence
